concepts.title: Cell: The Basic Unit of Life

questions.q: Why is the cell called the building block of life?
questions.a: All organisms are built of cells, and each cell carries out life's functions.

questions.q: Can we see cells with naked eyes? How do we see them?
questions.a: Most are too small; we use microscopes, and stains make parts visible.

questions.q: Name two things every cell contains.
questions.a: A cell membrane and cytoplasm (plants and animals cells also hold a nucleus).

concepts.title: Levels of Organisation in Living Bodies

questions.q: Arrange in order: organ, cell, organism, tissue, organ system.
questions.a: Cell -> tissue -> organ -> organ system -> organism.
A group of similar cells doing one job, like muscle tissue or blood.

questions.q: Give one example each of an organ and an organ system.
questions.a: Organ: heart. Organ system: digestive system.
Living things too small to see unaided - bacteria, viruses, fungi and protozoa.

questions.q: Name one microorganism useful to us and one harmful.
questions.a: Useful: yeast in bread. Harmful: virus causing flu (or cholera bacteria).
Almost everywhere - air, water, soil, inside and on our bodies.

concepts.title: Our Connection with Microbes: Use and Harm

questions.q: How do microbes help us in food making?
questions.a: Yeast makes dough rise, bacteria turn milk to curd, and fermentation makes idli batter fluffy.

questions.q: Name two diseases caused by microbes.
How does vaccination protect us from microbes?
questions.a: A weakened microbe teaches the body's defence to fight the real disease later.
